minutes.headline: Parks Commission put off the skate park joint meeting and field fee decision; two members approved minutes.
minutes.summary: Only two commissioners attended the remote meeting, so most items were postponed until a third member and the recreation director could join. The commission approved minutes, named a representative to the open space committee, and agreed to wait on a joint meeting about the skate park at the TC Passios site. Discussion covered Marshall Park ideas, a demolition moratorium versus a policy, DPW care of park properties, and new agenda items.

what_happened.line: Only two commissioners attended the remote meeting, so most items were postponed until a third member and the recreation director could join.
The commission deferred the skate park joint meeting with the skate park group and Selectmen until the third member and new members are in place.
By roll call, both members present voted for the chair to serve as the Parks representative on the open space committee.
Decision on 2020 field usage fees was tabled: fees are to be presented next month and decided in October.
Commissioners agreed to explore a demolition moratorium within a policy document and to add DPW care of parks to a future agenda.

why_it_matters: Field usage fees and the skate park site, both of which affect what residents pay to use and where they can use town recreation space, stay undecided until at least October.

A member's remarks that unspent parks money returns to free cash and that a full-time grounds position may need budget support point to a possible future request in the parks budget, which Town Meeting voters would be asked to fund.
